name: The generation of the Flood
charge: Corruption and violence filling the earth
summary: A whole world under judgment. The earth was filled with violence and every imagination of the heart was continually evil, so God resolved to blot out what he had made, sparing only Noah's household.
offense: God saw that the wickedness of man was great and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually. The earth was corrupt before him and filled with violence (Genesis 6:5-13). The judgment addressed both inward intention and outward harm: corrupt thoughts had become a corrupt way of life. Christ later recalled people eating, drinking, and marrying until the day Noah entered the ark (Matthew 24:37-39). Ordinary activity continued around an extraordinary warning. The danger was not that a meal or marriage was itself the offense named in Genesis, but that people continued without heeding the judgment coming upon their wickedness. God's longsuffering while the ark was preparing did not mean that the warning had been withdrawn (1 Peter 3:20).
judgment: All in whose nostrils was the breath of life upon the dry land died, and Noah only remained alive with those who were in the ark (Genesis 7:21-23). Peter identifies the preserved household as eight souls (1 Peter 3:20). The waters that bore up the ark overtook the world outside it; provision had to be received before the destruction came.

entries.commentary: The men who began to multiply on the face of the earth were of the other nations; they were not the direct descendants of Adam. The sons of God are the lineage of Adam laid out in chapter 5; that is the distinction between the sons of God and the daughters of men. The law against marrying into the other nations began here in Genesis. It was already known, and Moses had to reiterate that same law to the children of Israel when they came over Jordan.
Here the Most High shortened the lifespan of man to a hundred and twenty years. In chapter 5 the forefathers lived seven, eight, and nine hundred years.

The giants in the earth came from the sons of God intermingling with the other nations, and the children born to them became mighty men of renown. The angels which kept not their first estate are these same men of [Genesis 6:4](/bible/genesis/6#v4); they came from the lineage of Adam, and their first estate was sons of God. Another word for angel is messenger.

Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord; he was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God. Without Noah none of us would be here; Shem, Ham, and Japheth repopulated the earth after the flood.
The ark was a literal boat, made of gopher wood.

At this time the animals were vegetarian; that is why the Most High explained to Noah to gather food for himself, for his family, and for the animals, and why the animals did not eat one another on the ark.

Noah did all that the Most High commanded him by faith. Up to that time rain had never been seen; it takes faith to build an ark for a thing that has never happened. While the ark was preparing, Noah was a preacher of righteousness, telling his people to repent, and the longsuffering of the Most High waited for them to repent. Eight souls were saved by water; the ones that were actually in the water died, so this is not talking about getting baptized. As Noah prepared the ark to the saving of his house, we must prepare our households for when Christ comes back; that takes the same faith. In the days of Noah they were eating, drinking, and marrying until Noah entered the ark and there was no more chance to repent; so shall the coming of the Son of man be. We have to put on the spirit of Noah.

The dietary law was not yet instituted, but the Most High had already defined what was a clean beast and what was an unclean beast, all the way back in Genesis; Moses reiterated that law to the children of Israel. Today this gets confused with the doctrine that says I can eat all things through Christ who strengthens me, and that is not true; the laws were instituted for us to discern between the unclean and the clean. The beasts went in male and female to keep seed alive upon the face of all the earth, so that they could repopulate once the earth dried up; nature itself tells you what we should and should not be doing.

Up until this point it had never rained on the earth; a mist went up from the earth and watered the ground. Understand the faith Noah had to have, being told to build an ark because it was going to rain, a thing that had never happened.

The great deep is the seas, the rivers, and the oceans. The windows of heaven are the sky, the firmament, and their opening is the rain. This is the first time it ever rained on the earth, and when the rain came it came with destruction.

This was the first time the Most High destroyed the earth for the wickedness that was being done. The flood came because they despised the commandments; destruction came because of sin. Of them that dwelt in the world only Noah and his household were left, of whom came all righteous men: through Shem's seed to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and through their line the Israelites. The breath of life is twofold. One is the commandments, which were given to Adam; the other is the breathing life, the oxygen. Here everything on the dry land that breathed died; the fish were not touched.

Of the buildings of the temple he says there shall not be left here one stone upon another that shall not be thrown down, and on the mount of Olives the disciples ask when, and what shall be the sign.

Take heed that no man deceive you. Many shall come in my name saying I am Christ, and shall deceive many. Wars and rumours of wars, nation against nation, famines, pestilences and earthquakes are all the beginning of sorrows, not the end.

Ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake, many shall be offended and betray one another, and because iniquity shall abound the love of many shall wax cold. He that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved. That verse alone answers any man who says he is already saved and has nothing left to endure.
This gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations, and then shall the end come.
The abomination of desolation spoken of by Daniel the prophet standing in the holy place. That has a fulfilment already in history, when swine's flesh was offered in the temple.

Then let them which be in Judaea flee into the mountains, and pray that the flight be not in the winter, neither on the sabbath day. Then shall be great tribulation such as was not since the beginning of the world, and except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved; but for the elect's sake those days shall be shortened.

False Christs and false prophets shall shew great signs and wonders, insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect. Go not forth after them. As the lightning cometh out of the east and shineth even unto the west, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.

Immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun shall be darkened, the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven. He shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds. That gathering is itself proof of a people scattered to the four winds.

Learn a parable of the fig tree: when his branch is yet tender and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh. So likewise when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors. Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.

Of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only. As the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be: eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, and they knew not until the flood came and took them all away.

Blessed is that servant whom his lord when he cometh shall find giving the household meat in due season, and he shall be made ruler over all his goods. The evil servant says in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming, and begins to smite his fellowservants; his lord comes in a day he looks not for him and appoints him his portion with the hypocrites. Watching is not only watching the prophecy come to pass. It is keeping a watchful eye on your own spirit, because what is not repented of is what a man will be judged for.

In the thirtieth year after the ruin of the city I was in Babylon, and lay troubled upon my bed, and my thoughts came up over my heart. I saw the desolation of Sion, and the wealth of them that dwelt at Babylon; and my spirit was sore moved, so that I began to speak words full of fear to the most High. Thou gavest a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee. Unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way, which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations. In process of time thou broughtest the flood upon those that dwelt in the world, and destroyedst them; nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men.

When they that dwelt upon the earth began to multiply, they began again to be more ungodly than the first. Thou didst choose thee a man from among them, whose name was Abraham: him thou lovedst, and made an everlasting covenant with him, promising him that thou wouldest never forsake his seed. Unto him thou gavest Isaac, and unto Isaac thou gavest Jacob and Esau: as for Jacob, thou didst choose him to thee, and put by Esau. When thou leddest his seed out of Egypt, thou broughtest them up to the mount Sinai, and bowing the heavens thou didst set fast the earth, and madest the depths to tremble. Thy glory went through four gates, of fire, and of earthquake, and of wind, and of cold; that thou mightest give the law unto the seed of Jacob, and diligence unto the generation of Israel.

Yet tookest thou not away from them a wicked heart, that thy law might bring forth fruit in them. For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him. Thus infirmity was made permanent; and the law also in the heart of the people with the malignity of the root; so that the good departed away, and the evil abode still. Thou raisedst up a servant, called David, whom thou commandedst to build a city unto thy name, and to offer incense and oblations unto thee therein. When this was done many years, then they that inhabited the city forsook thee, and in all things did even as Adam and all his generations had done; and so thou gavest the city over into the hands of thine enemies.

Are their deeds any better that inhabit Babylon, that they should therefore have the dominion over Sion? When I came thither, and had seen impieties without number, then my soul saw many evildoers in this thirtieth year, so that my heart failed me. I have seen how thou sufferest them sinning, and hast spared the wicked doers, and hast destroyed thy people, and hast preserved thine enemies. Are they then of Babylon better than they of Sion? or is there any other people that knoweth thee beside Israel? or what generation hath so believed thy covenants as Jacob? For I have gone here and there through the heathen, and I see that they flow in wealth, and think not upon thy commandments. Weigh thou therefore our wickedness now in the balance, and theirs also that dwell in the world; and so shall thy name no where be found but in Israel. Thou shalt find that Israel by name hath kept thy precepts, but not the heathen. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

verses.text: And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.
And it repented the Lord that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart.
And the Lord said, I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth; both man, and beast, and the creeping thing, and the fowls of the air; for it repenteth me that I have made them.
The earth also was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.
And God looked upon the earth, and, behold, it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth.
And God said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth.
And all flesh died that moved upon the earth, both of fowl, and of cattle, and of beast, and of every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth, and every man:
All in whose nostrils was the breath of life, of all that was in the dry land, died.

And every living substance was destroyed which was upon the face of the ground, both man, and cattle, and the creeping things, and the fowl of the heaven; and they were destroyed from the earth: and Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark.
And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly;
But as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.
For as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark,
And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.
For whose cause the earth being drowned with the flood, wisdom again preserved it, and directed the course of the righteous in a piece of wood of small value.
And every people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before thee, and despised thy commandments.
And again in process of time thou broughtest the flood upon those that dwelt in the world, and destroyedst them.
And it came to pass in every of them, that as death was to Adam, so was the flood to these.
He was not pacified toward the old giants, who fell away in the strength of their foolishness.
